ContributorJourneyOneDesc: Your journey begins when your employer registers you as an employee under their establishment.
ContributorJourneyTwoDesc: Documents your employment and contribution history with GOSI, enabling you to obtain a certificate showing your contribution record and contributory wage.
ContributorJourneyThreeDesc: You can update your personal and contact information to ensure accurate delivery of all services and communications.
ContributorJourneyFourDesc: You can review your contribution periods and submit requests to add or modify incomplete periods to ensure your rights are calculated accurately.
ContributorJourneyFiveDesc: Your contribution with GOSI ends when you leave your job, and resumes automatically once you join a new employer.
ContributorJourneySixDesc: At the end of your career and upon retirement, we process and disburse your retirement pension.
ContributorJourneySevenDesc: If you are not eligible for a retirement pension, you may request a lump-sum payment in accordance with the regulations.
HeirsJourneyOneDesc: The beneficiary’s journey begins when they become eligible for the pension due to the contributor’s death. The deceased’s pension is proactively suspended in coordination with the National Information Center to ensure the rights of the beneficiary and their family, and to guarantee that the pension is paid only to eligible dependents.

HeirsJourneyTwoDesc: Your benefits as an eligible heir are disbursed immediately after the contributor’s death, and you may then issue a certificate showing the pension amount.
HeirsJourneyThree: Issuing a Pension Amount Certificate for Heirs
HeirsJourneyThreeDesc: This service allows heirs to issue a certificate that states the pension amount.
HeirsJourneyFourDesc: When a change occurs in marital, educational, health, or employment status or when reporting the birth of a new child you can add them as a beneficiary to the pension.
HeirsJourneyFiveDesc: You can report any change in marital, educational, health, or employment status to protect beneficiaries’ rights and ensure uninterrupted benefit disbursement.
HeirsJourneySixDesc: The heir can update their personal or banking information to ensure continuous and accurate disbursement of the pension.
EstablishmentJourneyOneDesc: The employer’s journey begins with registering the establishment through government integration channels, except for government, semi-government, international, and regional entities, whose registration requires submitting an official request to GOSI. The establishment’s information is then verified, and its account is created in Social Insurance, enabling the employer to manage insurance-related obligations electronically with ease.
EstablishmentJourneyTwoDesc: After registration, the employer moves on to managing the establishment’s account, which includes three main stages:
EstablishmentJourneyTwoADesc: The employer manages the establishment’s information, such as updating ownership details, modifying the legal entity, and managing branches to ensure data accuracy and service continuity.
EstablishmentJourneyTwoBDesc: The employer registers new workers, updates their wages, transfers them between branches when needed, or excludes them upon termination of service—ensuring their full insurance protection.
EstablishmentJourneyTwoCDesc: The employer monitors the establishment’s financial obligations through the dashboard, pays outstanding amounts electronically, and can transfer balances between branches with ease and flexibility.
EstablishmentJourneyThreeDesc: The journey concludes when the establishment’s activity ends. The data is automatically received through government integration channels, and all insurance obligations are verified before approving the closure and completing the activity termination process officially.

MaternityBenefitDes: Protection and Security for Working Mothers
MaternityBenefitDes2: Social Insurance (GOSI) provides female employees with compensation on behalf of their employer when they take leave from work due to childbirth. This benefit is available to contributors under the Occupational Hazards Branch in both the current and new Social Insurance Law, whether the contributor is Saudi or non-Saudi.
PaidForThreeMonth: It is paid for a period of 3 months, with an additional month added in certain cases.
RestrictionWithSalary: It cannot be received alongside the regular salary.
StartFromFirstMonth: It takes effect starting from the first month in which childbirth occurs.
MinimumLimitOneYear: It applies if the contributor is actively employed and has completed at least 12 months of contributions within the 36 months preceding the childbirth date.
SupportEmployer: It supports employers by alleviating their financial burdens.
EnhanceSustainability: It enhances the establishment’s stability by fostering a balanced and sustainable work relationship.
WorkBalance: It promotes balance between professional and family life.

Occupational disability is a permanent total or partial disability resulting from a work-related injury.
 In such cases, the injured individual is entitled to either continuous or lump-sum compensation in accordance with the provisions of the Social Insurance Law. 
Occupational disability beneficiaries represent a portion of the total beneficiaries covered under the Occupational Hazards branch
